name: coordinator-single-writer
body:
The session coordinator is the single writer of the worktree DB AND of the durable mutation. While a session is live it owns `apg/.trans/db.lbug` exclusively (one writer → no concurrent lbug open) AND it performs the whole durable write itself — the node-file read-modify-write (e.g. `edge_add`'s read-push-write on the source file, src/node_cmd.rs:207, and `node_rm`'s rewrite of every referencing file), the one-commit-per-mutation commit (`git::commit_files`), and the projection record — applying routed mutations in the order it receives them. Owning only the DB is NOT enough: if clients keep writing/committing node files directly, two parallel `edge add`s on the same source still lose an edge and two commits still contend on `.git/index.lock`, and the "store equals the serial application" acceptance cannot hold. The coordinator therefore owns the read-modify-write, not merely the DB open. Any other would-be writer either routes through the session or waits.

Reads while the session is live: `apg query` and the suite query tools do not write, so they are not serialized by the single writer — but they must obtain their view by ROUTING through the live session (read-through, `read-access-during-session`); routed reads are served by the session and keep working transparently. This scoping is load-bearing: lbug's contended open ERRORS ("Could not set lock") rather than waits, so a reader that opens `db.lbug` directly during a live session is out of contract and must route or be retried after the session ends. Only routed read-only readers are promised continued service; a direct non-routing open is not. Acceptance: with a live session, no competing process opens the DB read-write and no client writes a node file directly (the session performs the RMW + commit); the resulting store equals the serial application of the same mutations; routed read-only reads (`apg query` / suite tools) still succeed.
